newsitem.title: SWEDEN: TENNIS-BATTLING ENQVIST BRINGS SWEDEN BACK INTO CUP. [CORRECTED 23:02 GMT]
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BATTLING ENQVIST BRINGS SWEDEN BACK INTO CUP. [CORRECTED 23:02 GMT]

text.p: Battling Thomas Enqvist kept Sweden's Davis Cup hopes alive on Sunday, clawing back from two sets down to beat Cedric Pioline and level the final against France 2-2.

Enqvist, the top ranked player in the final at number nine in the world, overcame an early shaky service, high tension and a fired-up Pioline to win the match 3-6 6-7 6-4 6-4 9-7 after nearly four and a half hours. (Corrects final set score from 8-6 to 9-7)

The lanky Enqvist fired in 22 aces, but he also had trouble keeping his first serve in and Pioline, playing as though his life depended on it until he lost concentration in the third set, pounced on every loose shot.

But the Swede kept his cool amid the deafening noise of rival supporters echoing round the huge converted factory hosting the tie. Yet all looked lost in the nailbiting final set when Pioline broke his serve in the second game.

But Enqvist pressured the Frenchman into groundstroke errors in the ninth and broke back. Pioline succumbed to nerves to lose his serve at 7-7 with a double fault and the Swede served out for the match.
